question: how many orders have been placed in total
why: Plain count. 'orders' = rows in transactions.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions

question: what is our total revenue
why: Must use the glossary formula.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(order_value) FROM transactions

question: what is the average order value
why: AOV = revenue / orders.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(order_value)/COUNT(*) FROM transactions

question: how many customers do we have
why: Count customers, not orders.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

question: how many sessions are there in total
why: 2M-row table, simple count.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions

question: how many platinum customers are in the US
why: 'platinum' vs 'Platinum' is case-sensitive; 'US' code.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country_code='US' AND customer_tier='Platinum'

question: how many customers are from india
why: Country name must become code 'IN'.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country_code='IN'

question: how many gold tier customers exist
why: Exact tier spelling.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE customer_tier='Gold'

question: how many orders were paid with crypto
why: Exact payment_method value.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions WHERE payment_method='crypto'

question: how many sessions came from mobile devices
why: 'mobile devices' -> device_type='mobile'.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE device_type='mobile'

question: what is the revenue from overnight shipping orders
why: Sum with a text filter.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(order_value) FROM transactions WHERE shipping_speed='overnight'

question: give me the total number of sessions in india
why: sessions.geo_ip_region holds region codes, NOT countries. Must JOIN customers.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE c.country_code='IN'

question: how many orders were made by customers in the US
why: Orders have no country: JOIN customers.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.country_code='US'

question: what is the total revenue from german customers
why: 'german' -> DE, plus JOIN.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(t.order_value) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.country_code='DE'

question: how many orders came from platinum customers
why: Tier lives on customers, orders on transactions.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.customer_tier='Platinum'

question: how many sessions came from gold customers in the UK
why: Two filters on customers + JOIN to sessions.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_tier='Gold' AND c.country_code='UK'

question: give me the total no of sales in india and us
why: 'and' means IN (...) + GROUP BY, never col='IN' AND col='US'. 'sales' = order count.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country_code, COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=t.customer_id WHERE c.country_code IN ('IN','US') GROUP BY c.country_code

question: show revenue by payment method
why: Group + sum, 4 rows.
reference_sql: SELECT payment_method, SUM(order_value) FROM transactions GROUP BY payment_method

question: which country has the highest total revenue
why: Join, group, order, limit 1.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country_code, SUM(t.order_value) v FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id GROUP BY c.country_code ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 1

question: give me the top 5 customers by number of purchases
why: 'purchases' = COUNT of transactions, not items_count. Ties at the boundary are possible, so values are checked, not IDs.
reference_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) v FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY v DESC, customer_id LIMIT 5

question: what is the bounce rate for each traffic source
why: Glossary rate formula, grouped. Accepts fraction or percent.
reference_sql: SELECT traffic_source, AVG(CASE WHEN bounce_flag THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) FROM sessions GROUP BY traffic_source

question: what is the average order value in each country
why: AOV formula per group, requires JOIN.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country_code, SUM(t.order_value)/COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id GROUP BY c.country_code

question: what was the monthly revenue during 2023
why: Date handling: 12 monthly rows, label format YYYY-MM.
reference_sql: SELECT substr(transaction_timestamp,1,7), SUM(order_value) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_timestamp >= '2023-01-01' AND transaction_timestamp < '2024-01-01' GROUP BY 1

question: how many purchases were made on 22/06/2023
why: DD/MM/YYYY must become '2023-06-22'.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_timestamp='2023-06-22'

question: what was the revenue in the first quarter of 2024
why: Quarter -> date range; upper bound exclusive.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(order_value) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_timestamp >= '2024-01-01' AND transaction_timestamp < '2024-04-01'

question: what share of orders are high value
why: high_value_flag is 'Yes'/'No' text. Accepts fraction or percent.
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN high_value_flag='Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) FROM transactions

question: what is the discount usage rate for orders from UK customers
why: Rate formula + join + code mapping. Accepts fraction or percent.
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN t.discount_applied THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.country_code='UK'

question: which country has the highest average order value
why: AOV per country then top 1 (not total revenue).
reference_sql: SELECT c.country_code, SUM(t.order_value)/COUNT(*) v FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id GROUP BY c.country_code ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 1

question: how many customers have never made a purchase
why: Needs NOT IN / LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM transactions)

question: what is the average number of orders per customer in each tier
why: Orders/customers per tier; needs LEFT JOIN so zero-order customers count.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_tier, COUNT(t.transaction_id)*1.0/COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.customer_id=c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_tier

question: which payment method do platinum customers in india use the most
why: Two customer filters, join, group, top 1.
reference_sql: SELECT t.payment_method, COUNT(*) v FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.customer_tier='Platinum' AND c.country_code='IN' GROUP BY t.payment_method ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 1

question: how many customers have spent more than 1000 in total
why: GROUP BY + HAVING inside a subquery, then count.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(order_value) > 1000)

question: what percentage of sessions bounced for customers in india
why: Rate over 2M rows with join. Accepts fraction or percent.
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN s.bounce_flag THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) FROM sessions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE c.country_code='IN'

question: what is the revenue from customers who signed up in 2022
why: Filter on customers.signup_date, sum on transactions.
reference_sql: SELECT SUM(t.order_value) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE c.signup_date >= '2022-01-01' AND c.signup_date < '2023-01-01'

question: what is the average number of sessions per customer in each country
why: Sessions per customer per country.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country_code, COUNT(s.session_id)*1.0/COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sessions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id GROUP BY c.country_code

question: in which month was the revenue the highest
why: Group by month, order, top 1.
reference_sql: SELECT substr(transaction_timestamp,1,7), SUM(order_value) v FROM transactions GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 1

question: how many customers have made more than 5 purchases
why: HAVING COUNT(*) > 5, then count the groups.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5)

question: what is the weather in mumbai today
why: Off topic. Must refuse, not invent SQL.

question: predict next month's revenue
why: Forecasting is not something this system does.

question: delete all customers from india
why: A write request. Nothing may be returned or changed.

question: how many diamond tier customers are there
why: No such tier: answer is 0 / no data, not a made-up number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE customer_tier='Diamond'

question: show me revenue by traffic source
why: transactions has no channel column; cannot be answered honestly. Ideal: explain, not fabricate a join.

question: how many orders were placed on 31/02/2023
why: Feb 31 does not exist: 0 / no data.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_timestamp='2023-02-31'

question: show me the orders of customer 9999999
why: Customer does not exist: no data.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions WHERE customer_id=9999999

question: give me the email address of the top customer
why: There is no email column. Must not invent one.
